s1.syndrome_frame: persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and indurated plaque on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
heterogeneously fluid hyperintense and T1 heterogeneously hyperintense lesion on MRI
mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition on pathology
key_facts: patient is a woman in her 30s
presented with a painful bruise on her hand
bruise appeared a few days after a twisting injury to the affected hand
injury occurred 2 years before presentation
bruise and pain persisted despite icing and resting the area
patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
radiography showed soft tissue swelling but was otherwise unremarkable
MRI showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense and T1 heterogeneously hyperintense lesion
pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

Giant cell tumor of soft tissue
per_call: Subcutaneous fat necrosis of the newborn
Giant cell tumor of soft tissue

shortlist.label: Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor (HFLT)
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and indurated plaque on the hand, and pathology results showing mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of a subcutaneous lesion with spindled cells and positive CD34 immunohistochemistry, although the absence of S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A staining reduces its likelihood

shortlist.label: Nora lesion
shortlist.why_kept: a rare tumor that can present as a painful subcutaneous nodule, although the clinical and pathological features are not as strongly matched as HFLT

shortlist.label: Plexiform fibrohistiocytic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: can present with a similar clinical appearance, but the pathology results do not strongly support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Dermatofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: a possible consideration due to the presence of a subcutaneous lesion with spindled cells, but the clinical and pathological features are not as well-matched as HFLT

raw.rationale: The pathology results showing mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, along with lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, and immunohistochemistry strongly positive for CD34, are consistent with HFLT. The clinical presentation of a painful bruise that persisted despite conservative management also aligns with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: While dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans can present with similar clinical features, the pathology results, particularly the presence of mature adipose tissue and extensive pigment deposition, are not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Nora lesion
rejected.why: Nora lesion typically presents as a painless, slow-growing nodule, which does not match the patient's symptoms of a painful bruise.

rejected.label: Plexiform fibrohistiocytic tumor
rejected.why: This tumor usually occurs in children and young adults, and its pathology is characterized by a plexiform arrangement of fibrohistiocytic cells, which is not described in the patient's pathology results.

rejected.label: Dermatofibroma
rejected.why: Dermatofibroma is a common benign skin tumor, but the patient's pathology results, including the presence of mature adipose tissue and extensive pigment deposition, are not typical for dermatofibroma.
